_about: Plain-English explainers for top ORC offenses on the Hamilton County Justice Center roster. These are summaries for laypeople, not legal advice. Each charge is an accusation only; no person counted here has been convicted.

2903.01.plain: Aggravated murder. Purposely killing another person with prior calculation, while committing certain felonies, or against specific protected victims.
2903.01.tier_meaning: F1 — life imprisonment, life without parole, or capital. Most serious offense in Ohio.

2903.02.plain: Murder. Purposely causing the death of another person. (Aggravated murder, 2903.01, adds prior calculation or aggravating factors.)
2903.02.tier_meaning: F1 — 15 years to life in prison.

2903.04.plain: Involuntary manslaughter. Causing death while committing another felony or misdemeanor — no intent to kill, but death resulted.

2903.06.plain: Aggravated vehicular homicide. Causing death while OVI, recklessly driving, or in flagrant violation of traffic law.

2903.11.plain: Felonious assault. Knowingly causing serious physical harm, OR causing harm by means of a deadly weapon. Brandishing a firearm at someone during an assault qualifies even without firing.

2903.13.plain: Assault. Knowingly causing or attempting to cause physical harm to another, OR recklessly causing serious physical harm. Bar fights, simple punches.
2903.13.tier_meaning: M1 — up to 180 days jail, $1,000 fine. Becomes a felony against certain victims (officers, EMS, teachers).

2903.18.plain: Strangulation. Knowingly impeding another person's breathing or blood circulation by applying pressure to the throat or neck, or covering nose and mouth. Distinct from broader assault because of how dangerous and predictive of future violence it is.

2903.21.plain: Aggravated menacing. Knowingly causing another to believe the offender will cause serious physical harm to them, a family member, or property. Threats credible enough to put someone in fear.
2903.21.tier_meaning: M1 — up to 180 days. F5 if victim is an officer.

2905.01.plain: Kidnapping. By force, threat, or deception, restraining the liberty of another to hold for ransom, use as shield, facilitate a felony, terrorize, or commit a sexual offense.

2907.02.plain: Rape. Engaging in sexual conduct with another by force or threat of force, or when the other person's ability to resist is substantially impaired. No statute of limitations in Ohio when DNA evidence exists.
2907.02.tier_meaning: F1 — 3 years to life. Mandatory prison.

2907.03.plain: Sexual battery. Sexual conduct under specific coercive or relational circumstances (custody, family, professional authority, etc.) — broader than rape, narrower than consensual.
2907.03.tier_meaning: F3 — typically 1-5 years. F2 if minor.

2911.01.plain: Aggravated robbery. Robbery (theft by force/fear) committed while having a deadly weapon, dangerous ordnance, or while inflicting/attempting serious physical harm.

2911.02.plain: Robbery. Theft committed by inflicting, attempting, or threatening physical harm — or fleeing with a stolen item. Distinct from theft because of the force element.

2911.11.plain: Aggravated burglary. Trespass by force/stealth/deception into an occupied structure to commit a criminal offense, while having a deadly weapon OR inflicting/attempting harm OR another person is present.

2911.12.plain: Burglary. Trespass by force/stealth/deception into an occupied structure to commit a criminal offense. Distinct from aggravated burglary by the absence of weapon, harm, or occupant.

2911.13.plain: Breaking and entering. Trespass by force/stealth/deception into an unoccupied structure to commit a theft or felony. Distinct from burglary which requires an occupied structure.

2911.21.plain: Criminal trespass. Knowingly entering or remaining on premises without authorization, after notice to leave, or against express posting/fence.

2913.02.plain: Theft. Knowingly obtaining or exerting control over another's property without consent, by deception, threat, or intimidation, with purpose to deprive. The tier escalates with the dollar value: under $1,000 is M1; $1,000-$7,500 is F5; up to F1 for $1.5M+.
2913.02.tier_meaning: M1 default — up to 180 days. Felony at $1,000+.

2913.51.plain: Receiving stolen property. Receiving, retaining, or disposing of property of another knowing (or having reasonable cause to believe) it has been obtained through commission of a theft offense.
2913.51.tier_meaning: M1 default — up to 180 days. Tier ladders with value, same as theft.

2913.31.plain: Forgery. Forging any writing of another, or uttering a writing one knows to have been forged, with purpose to defraud.

2917.11.plain: Disorderly conduct. Recklessly causing inconvenience, annoyance, or alarm — fighting, threatening, insulting communication, unreasonable noise. The state's lowest tier of public-order offense.
2917.11.tier_meaning: MM — fine only, no jail unless persistent (then M4).

2919.025.plain: Domestic violence. This code is a local Hamilton County Sheriff's Office variant of 2919.25. It covers knowingly causing or attempting to cause physical harm to a family or household member.

2919.25.plain: Domestic violence. Knowingly causing or attempting to cause physical harm to a family or household member, OR recklessly causing serious harm, OR by threat causing belief of imminent harm.
2919.25.tier_meaning: M1 default — escalates with priors (F5 → F3 → F1 with prior convictions).

2919.27.plain: Violating a protection order. Recklessly violating the terms of a protection order, consent agreement, or anti-stalking order issued by a court.
2919.27.tier_meaning: M1 default. Escalates to F5/F3 with priors or while committing another offense.

2921.12.plain: Tampering with evidence. Altering, destroying, or concealing a thing with purpose to impair its availability as evidence — OR making/presenting false evidence.

2921.31.plain: Obstructing official business. Without privilege, doing any act that hampers or impedes a public official in performance of lawful duties. Refusing to identify, fleeing a stop, blocking arrest of another.
2921.31.tier_meaning: M2 default — up to 90 days. F5 if it creates risk of physical harm.

2921.33.plain: Resisting arrest. Recklessly or by force resisting/interfering with a lawful arrest of self or another.
2921.33.tier_meaning: M2 default — up to 90 days. F4 with weapon, F3 with harm to officer.

2921.331.plain: Failure to comply with order/signal of police officer. Operating a motor vehicle so as to wilfully elude or flee a police officer after receiving visible/audible signal to stop. Pursuits.
2921.331.tier_meaning: M1 default — up to 180 days. F3-F4 with risk of harm.

2921.38.plain: Harassment with a bodily substance. Causing/attempting to cause an officer, employee of detention facility, or other to come into contact with blood, semen, urine, feces, or other bodily substance.
2921.38.tier_meaning: F5 default. F3 if HIV/HepB/HepC positive and discloses.

2923.12.plain: Carrying concealed weapons. Knowingly carrying or having concealed about one's person any deadly weapon or dangerous ordnance. Lawful with valid CCW permit; not so without.
2923.12.tier_meaning: M1 default — up to 180 days. F4 if dangerous ordnance / loaded firearm in CCW-prohibited place.

2923.13.plain: Having weapons while under disability. Knowingly acquiring/possessing a firearm or dangerous ordnance while under a legal disability — prior felony of violence, drug conviction, mental commitment, fugitive status.

2923.161.plain: Improperly discharging a firearm at or into a habitation or school zone. Knowingly discharging a firearm at/into an occupied structure or school safety zone.

2925.03.plain: Trafficking in drugs. Knowingly selling/offering to sell a controlled substance, OR preparing for shipment/distribution/transport when knowing it'll be sold. Distinct from possession by intent/conduct toward sale.
2925.03.tier_meaning: F5 default. Ladders by substance/weight up to F1.

2925.11.plain: Possession of drugs. Knowingly obtaining, possessing, or using a controlled substance or controlled substance analog. The most common felony charge in Hamilton County.
2925.11.tier_meaning: F5 default for most schedules. Ladders by substance/weight up to F1.

2925.14.plain: Illegal use or possession of drug paraphernalia. Knowingly using, possessing with intent to use, drug paraphernalia (e.g., pipes, scales, baggies designed/used for controlled substances).
2925.14.tier_meaning: MM — fine only, no jail unless involving a minor (then M2).

4510.16.plain: Driving on a suspended/revoked license. Operating a motor vehicle while one's driving privileges are suspended or revoked, knowing of the suspension/revocation.
4510.16.tier_meaning: M1 default — up to 180 days. Tier escalates with priors.

4511.19.plain: Operating a vehicle under the influence (OVI / DUI). Operating any vehicle under the influence of alcohol, drugs, or both; or with prohibited concentration in breath/blood/urine.
4511.19.tier_meaning: M1 default — minimum 3 days jail, up to 180 days. Ladders sharply with priors / felony OVI at 4 priors / 10 yrs.

4549.02.plain: Stopping after accident on public roads (leaving the scene). Driver involved in a collision must stop, exchange info, and render aid. Failure to do so is criminal.
4549.02.tier_meaning: M1 default — up to 180 days. F5 with injury, F3 with death.

2909.06.plain: Criminal damaging or endangering. Knowingly or recklessly causing physical harm to another person's property without their consent.
2909.06.tier_meaning: M2 default — up to 90 days; M1 (up to 180 days) if it risked physical harm to a person or was done by fire or explosion.

4510.12.plain: Operating a motor vehicle without a valid license (never licensed, or license expired). Distinct from driving under suspension, where a license was taken away.
4510.12.tier_meaning: Unclassified/MM first offense — fine; up to M1 (180 days) with priors.

2925.12.plain: Possessing drug abuse instruments. Knowingly making, obtaining, or using an instrument such as a hypodermic or syringe to unlawfully administer a dangerous drug.
2925.12.tier_meaning: M2 default — up to 90 days; M1 with a prior drug-related conviction.

2923.02.plain: Attempt. Purposely engaging in conduct that would complete an offense if the circumstances were as the person believed. The penalty is set one degree below the offense attempted.
2923.02.tier_meaning: One degree lower than the completed offense (e.g., attempted F2 is an F3; attempted M1 is an M2).
2923.02.max_term: One degree below the target offense

2921.13.plain: Falsification. Knowingly making a false statement, or swearing to the truth of one, to mislead a public official or in an official proceeding.
2921.13.tier_meaning: M1 default — up to 180 days; rises to a felony in specific circumstances (e.g., to obtain certain benefits).

4510.11.plain: Driving under suspension or in violation of a license restriction. Operating a vehicle while the license is suspended for a non-OVI reason such as points, a financial-responsibility action, or a court order.
4510.11.tier_meaning: M1 default — up to 180 days, with mandatory license actions on conviction.

4511.202.plain: Operating a motor vehicle without being in reasonable control of it. Often charged after a single-vehicle crash or loss of control.
4511.202.tier_meaning: MM — minor misdemeanor, fine only, no jail.

2921.29.plain: Failure to disclose personal information. Refusing to give your name, address, or date of birth to a peace officer who is investigating a crime and has lawfully detained you.

4513.263.plain: Occupant restraining devices. Operating or riding in a vehicle without wearing a required seat belt. Enforced as a secondary offense.
4513.263.tier_meaning: Minor offense — fine only, no jail and no license points.

2923.16.plain: Improperly handling firearms in a motor vehicle. Transporting or having a loaded or accessible firearm in a vehicle outside the law's allowances, or being armed while under the influence.
2923.16.tier_meaning: Ranges from M1 to felony (commonly F4-F3) depending on whether the firearm was loaded, accessible, and concealed-carry status.

2903.22.plain: Menacing. Knowingly causing another person to believe you will cause physical harm to them, their family, or their property.
2903.22.tier_meaning: M4 default — up to 30 days; rises (to M1, then felony) for protected victims or with priors.

4301.62.plain: Open container of beer or intoxicating liquor. Having an open container in a public place or in the passenger area of a motor vehicle.
4301.62.tier_meaning: Minor misdemeanor — fine only, no jail.

2919.22.plain: Endangering children. Creating a substantial risk to a child's health or safety by violating a duty of care, protection, or support, or by excessive discipline.
2919.22.tier_meaning: M1 default — up to 180 days; rises to a felony (F3/F2) when serious physical harm results.
2919.22.max_term: Up to 180 days (M1); felony with serious harm

4511.21.plain: Speed limits. Driving faster than is reasonable for the conditions, or exceeding the posted limit.
4511.21.tier_meaning: Minor misdemeanor — fine only; escalates to M4/M3 with repeat offenses within a year.

2913.03.plain: Unauthorized use of a vehicle. Knowingly using someone's vehicle, boat, or aircraft without consent. Less than theft because there is no intent to permanently deprive.
2913.03.tier_meaning: M1 default — up to 180 days; F5 if kept beyond 48 hours or removed from the state.

4510.111.plain: Driving under a non-compliance suspension. Operating a vehicle while the license is suspended for failing to meet a requirement such as proof of insurance or a court obligation.
4510.111.tier_meaning: Unclassified/M1 — fine and possible jail up to 180 days.

2923.162.plain: Discharge of a firearm on or near prohibited premises. Firing a gun upon or over a public road or other prohibited area.
2923.162.tier_meaning: Felony — commonly F3, rising to F1 if it causes serious physical harm.

2907.05.plain: Gross sexual imposition. Sexual contact compelled by force, enabled by drugs, with a person unable to consent, or with a child under 13.
2907.05.tier_meaning: Felony — F4 default, F3 when the victim is a child under 13.

2923.24.plain: Possessing criminal tools. Possessing any device, substance, or instrument with the purpose to use it criminally.
2923.24.tier_meaning: M1 default — up to 180 days; F5 when the intended crime is a felony.

4510.14.plain: Driving under an OVI suspension. Operating a vehicle while the license is suspended for a prior impaired-driving (OVI) offense.
4510.14.tier_meaning: M1 — mandatory minimum jail, escalating with priors.

2907.322.plain: Pandering sexually oriented matter involving a minor. Creating, reproducing, or distributing material showing a minor in sexual activity.

2905.03.plain: Unlawful restraint. Knowingly restraining another of their liberty, without the aggravating factors of kidnapping or abduction.

2909.07.plain: Criminal mischief. Tampering with or interfering with another's property, or with public utilities or safety devices.
2909.07.tier_meaning: M3 default — up to 60 days; rises with risk or value.

2909.05.plain: Vandalism. Knowingly causing serious physical harm to property that is occupied, used in a business, or government-owned.
2909.05.tier_meaning: Felony — F5 default, rising with the dollar value of harm.

2907.09.plain: Public indecency. Recklessly exposing one's private parts, or engaging in sexual conduct, in view of others.
2907.09.tier_meaning: MM to M1 depending on circumstances and priors (higher when a minor is present).

2923.15.plain: Using weapons while intoxicated. Carrying or using a firearm or dangerous ordnance while under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

2917.21.plain: Telecommunications harassment. Making a phone, text, or electronic communication to abuse, threaten, or harass another person.
2917.21.tier_meaning: M1 default — up to 180 days; F5 with a prior conviction.

4511.20.plain: Reckless operation. Operating a vehicle in willful or wanton disregard of the safety of persons or property.
4511.20.tier_meaning: Minor misdemeanor first offense; M4/M3 with priors.
4511.20.max_term: Fine; up to 60 days with priors

4511.33.plain: Driving in marked lanes. Failing to stay within a single marked lane or to change lanes safely.

2909.02.plain: Aggravated arson. Knowingly creating a substantial risk of serious physical harm to a person, or harming an occupied structure, by fire or explosion.

2921.34.plain: Escape. Purposely breaking or leaving detention, or failing to return to it, without authority.
2921.34.tier_meaning: Felony — degree tracks the underlying offense (commonly F2-F5).

4503.21.plain: Failure to display license plates. Operating a vehicle without properly displaying valid plates or validation stickers.

2921.36.plain: Illegal conveyance into a detention facility. Bringing weapons, drugs, or other prohibited items into a jail or prison.

4510.21.plain: Driving under a financial-responsibility suspension. Operating a vehicle while the license is suspended for failing to maintain proof of insurance.

4511.12.plain: Failure to obey a traffic control device. Disregarding a posted sign, signal, or pavement marking.

2917.31.plain: Inducing panic. Causing public alarm by a false report (fire, crime, emergency) or a threat.
2917.31.tier_meaning: M1 default — up to 180 days; felony when it causes economic harm or involves certain threats.

2905.02.plain: Abduction. Knowingly restraining or removing another by force or threat, creating a risk of physical harm or fear.

2903.211.plain: Menacing by stalking. A pattern of conduct that knowingly causes another to believe the offender will cause physical harm or mental distress.
2903.211.tier_meaning: M1 default — up to 180 days; F4 with aggravating factors or priors.

2913.21.plain: Misuse of credit cards. Using, obtaining, or trafficking in a credit card without consent or to defraud.
2913.21.tier_meaning: M1 default — up to 180 days; felony as the amount rises.

2950.06.plain: Failure to verify a registered address. A sex-offender registrant failing to periodically verify their residence as required.
2950.06.tier_meaning: Felony — degree tracks the underlying registration tier.

4503.11.plain: Failure to register a motor vehicle. Operating or parking an unregistered vehicle on a public road.
